title: Autoscale Scenarios Runbook for Failure-Mode Rehearsals
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a practical, testable runbook covering autoscale failure modes for Dedicated pools. The runbook will catalog likely failure scenarios (e.g., broker stalls, burst queueing, node OOM, KV cache blowups), define detection signals, play-by-play remediation steps, and a rehearsal schedule that ties into the quarterly capacity OKR. The deliverable includes a lightweight automation checklist (scripts/alerts), a Canary script for deliberate degradation, and runbook pages for on-call SREs and Customer Success engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook pages published in Confluence and linked from the Console runbook menu
Three failure-mode tabletop rehearsals executed with postmortem notes and action items
Alerting thresholds and runbook trigger links implemented in PagerDuty / Opsgenie
Canary automation can intentionally reduce pool capacity by 20% and validate fallback routing in <5m
Metrics dashboard (latency, tail p95/p99, queue length, cache hit rate) created and accessible to SRE/PM/DS
updates: 2025-02-10: Kickoff with SRE, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed scope: 6 core failure modes + 2 customer-impact scenarios.
2025-02-14: Draft detection signals mapped to existing alerts (ENG-4211) — added p99 token latency > 200ms sustained for 3m as primary signal.
2025-02-18: First tabletop (internal) run. Observed unclear ownership between Runtime and Routing for fallback activation — added explicit handoff step in runbook.
2025-02-21: Canary automation prototype (script v0.2) reduced pool by 15% and exercised model fallback; saw increased KV cache miss rate and transient errors on clients — captured as risk R-12.
2025-02-25: PM review with Customer Success: prioritized automations for customer-visible incidents (fail open vs. fail closed). Decided to default to fail-open for low-SLA plans.
2025-02-28: Draft runbook pushed to DraftConfluence PR. Requested runtime engineering review and telemetry owners to add run links.
decisions: Default fallback policy for Dedicated pools during partial capacity loss: route to compatible model variant (quantized/cheaper) rather than queue requests.
Runbook will include playbooks for both automated remediation (preferred) and manual escalation paths.
Canary exercises scheduled quarterly and must include at least one customer-impact scenario with a staging customer pool.
Failure rehearsals will be recorded and summarized into a 1-page runbook changelog for on-call rotation handoffs.
risks: Risk R-12: Canary-induced KV cache miss storms could temporarily increase per-token cost for other customers if not rate-limited.
Coordination overhead: requires SRE, Runtime, Console, and CS to be staffed for rehearsals (calendar conflicts risk).
False positives: poorly tuned detection thresholds may trigger runbook unnecessarily and cause unneeded failovers.
next_steps: Finalize detection thresholds with Runtime metrics team (ENG-8723).
Complete automation scripts and add safeguards to limit canary impact to a single dedicated pool.
Schedule two rehearsal windows (internal + staging customer) in March cycle and book SRE rotation coverage.
Assign owners for runbook maintenance and integration into Console (link + quick-run buttons).
notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing the DraftConfluence PR please focus on: 1) clarity of escalation ownership, 2) safety limits for canary scripts, 3) completeness of detection signals. Suggest concrete metric thresholds rather than vague language.
